Dec 1 10:00 JOLTS, Dec 4 08:30 payrolls; MRVL Dec 1 and CRM/SNOW Dec 2 test the AI trade next week
market.if_then: If QQQ trades below 633.93, Wednesday's close, in the first hour, then make no new buys today and leave any open orders below the market.

stocks.headline: Nvidia has paused server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia under tighter US rules on chips reaching China. It closed at 149.3 and is down 30.7% in 20 days.
stocks.why: Washington is closing the routes Chinese buyers used to get Nvidia chips through Southeast Asia, and a new rule makes buyers rule out Chinese renters. The 151.22 late-Wednesday price came before this news, so expect a weaker start than the market. The business itself is strong: sales are up 106%, forecasts are up 28% in 90 days, and it trades at 9 times next year's profit. The questions over leadership and governance keep big buyers cautious. The pause also weighs on server makers (SMCI), on memory (MU) and on TSM.

long_term.reason: The business is the cheapest it has been in 5 years against its profits. But export rules and the governance questions keep cutting into what investors will pay, so this is not the time to add.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A close back above 159.92 with the export news absorbed would turn this into Add on dips; a break below 124.5 would mean the market is pricing lost sales, not a panic.
stocks.action: Don't buy today; expect it to lag the rest of tech, and only consider adding near 124.5.

levels.means: above = the sell-off is over; below = still a falling stock
above = the export news is shrugged off; below = sellers in control
above = Wednesday's floor holds; below = the path opens to 124.5

stocks.if_then: If it trades above 151.22 after the first hour, then drop the bet against it and stand aside.

stocks.headline: Oracle fell 5.1% to 103.88 on Wednesday, just above its 52-week low of 99.34. It traded at 105.84 late Wednesday.
stocks.why: Investors are selling the companies that borrow and spend heavily to build AI data centers, and Oracle is the clearest example. The business does not look broken: it has $664.0B of signed contracts, sales growth sped up to 30%, and it trades at 9.4 times next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. The real risk is what it costs to build the capacity behind those contracts. The Dec 14 report has to show that spending is under control, because analysts already expect profit per share to be lower than a year ago. A strong Oracle print would also lift CRWV and the AI-infrastructure group.

long_term.reason: This matches the app's 'Buy now' view. The signed contracts and the low valuation outweigh the build-out risk at this price.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A close below 99.34, or a December report that shows the contracts slipping or spending running away, would move it to Wait.
stocks.action: Don't buy the open; buy a first half-position only if it trades at 105.84 or higher, and keep the rest for the Dec 14 report.

levels.means: above = the sell-off has reversed; below = still in repair
above = buyers defend Wednesday's close; below = no buy today
above = the 52-week low holds; below = exit today's buy

stocks.if_then: If it trades below 99.34, then sell today's buy and wait for the Dec 14 report.
